name: Ain Sokhna FSRU Gas Import Pipeline (Sonker berth to national grid)

values.PipelineName: Ain Sokhna FSRU Gas Import Pipeline
values.StartLocation: Sonker berth, Ain Sokhna Port (FSRU regasification berth)
values.EndLocation: National gas grid interconnection, Ain Sokhna
values.RouteNotes: Short onshore import connector (~17 km, 36-inch) laid by Petrojet/GASCO from the Sonker FSRU berth at Ain Sokhna to the national gas transmission grid; three new valve rooms. No official GIS located; endpoints from ministry inspection reporting.

researcher_notes: Match check: no existing Egypt gas row references Ain Sokhna, Sonker, SUMED, or an FSRU grid connector (57 rows in discovery_context.json reviewed) -> genuine miss, not matched_existing. Add-threshold met: (a) sponsor = GASCO (Egyptian Natural Gas Company, transmission operator) engineering/PM + Petrojet construction, EGAS state programme; (b) endpoints = Sonker FSRU berth, Ain Sokhna -> national gas grid, Suez governorate, Egypt; (c) concrete step = pipeline built 2024-2025, petroleum-minister site inspection May 2025, three valve rooms and 36-in/17-km line under active construction for the summer-2025 FSRU tie-in. Specs (36-inch dia, 17 km, three valve rooms) come from the May-2025 ministerial inspection reported by Daily News Egypt and Amwal Al Ghad -> SAME press event, so treated as one source, not two independent -> tier MEDIUM for the dimensional data. Existence and operating status are independently corroborated: Egypt Independent (2025-07-06) and Egypt Oil & Gas (Madbouly) both report the Sonker + SUMED FSRUs (Energos Power at Sonker, Energos Eskimo/Hoegh Galleon at SUMED) being connected to and feeding the national grid for peak-summer 2025; by July 2026 the three Ain Sokhna FSRUs are reported operating, hence Status=operating (was 'nearing grid connection' June 2025; construction is the conservative fallback if reviewer prefers). Borderline terminal-connector call: at 36-inch x 17 km with valve rooms and a distinct grid tie-in this is a substantial transmission connector worth a pipeline row (comparable to existing short Egyptian connectors like Idku-Abu Hummus / Damietta-SEGAS), so classed new_row rather than folded into the terminal entry. Entity caution: Owner=GASCO is the EGYPTIAN Natural Gas Company; entity_lookup returned only Norwegian 'Gassco' (ID 90) as a near match -- do NOT link this row to ID 90; GASCO Egypt is a separate entity (parent: Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Company / EGAS). Owner is inferred from GASCO's builder/transmission-operator role (no source states legal ownership explicitly) -> low confidence on ownership specifically. Capacity, cost, and precise route/GIS unavailable; RouteAccuracy=approximate, no route staged (geometry -> routes repo). All 5 cited URLs passed scripts/url_verifier.py. All sources English (source_language=en); no Arabic-only corroboration needed given English coverage.
